sections.skill: Size and build a business cash reserve

questions.prompt: What is a cash reserve?

choices.text: Money set aside for slow months and surprises
Money used for the owner's vacation
Money spent on advertising and promotions each month

questions.correct_answer: Money set aside for slow months and surprises
questions.intro: A CASH RESERVE (emergency fund) is money the business keeps aside for slow months, repairs or late payments. A common planning approach is to save enough to cover a set number of months of essential expenses, such as 2 to 3 months; this is a planning assumption, not a rule. Build it gradually, for example by moving a percentage of each sale into a separate savings account. Use it only for real emergencies, then refill it. Without a reserve, one surprise can force expensive borrowing.

sections.skill: Saving a percent until a goal

questions.prompt: 10 percent of 3,000 dollars is what?
questions.intro: To see how long a savings goal takes, find how much you save each period, then divide the goal by that amount. Example: save 10 percent of 2,000 dollars of monthly sales = 200 dollars a month. A 1,200-dollar goal takes 1,200 / 200 = 6 months. If the answer is not whole, round up to the next full month.
